content.body:
Originally designed as an exploitation tank, the Sherman M4A2 had excellent reliability, good speed and a 75mm gun with excellent HE rounds. Unfortunately, due to the odd US doctrine that declared that enemy tanks were to be fought only with tank destroyers, little attention was paid to the Shermans AT capability, which was not fantastic due to a low velocity AP round. Despite this, it became the standard Allied tank by 1944. In combat it had a good turret speed but a very high silhouette ... when it was first proposed, it should have dominated the battlefield with some reservations regarding it's ability against thick armour, but by the time it was deployed, its 75mm gun was distinctly outclassed by every other nation's similar 75mm weapons and various crash programs were started to rectify this urgently.
Control Variations: Driver spawns in buttoned. May use periscope, or unbutton with O key. Driver has gauge showing turret facing relative to vehicle, driver's normal gauges not even peripherally visible unless you press numpad 0 or Ins key to deliberately look at them. Gunner has no view slit, no range adjustment (gradations only). Crew 4 is radioman, has hull mg with no crosshair at all. Can unbutton with O key and still fire hull mg.
Despite its shortcomings, the Sherman is a decent medium tank. The high silhouette does pose a big target; conversely it improves visibility on the battlefield for the commander and it's much easier to find a hull-down position and still fire over the protection of the berm in front of your hull. Expect that you will be outranged in gun duels against 75mm-armed tanks employed by the German forces. Work in teams and use cover to keep encounter ranges short where possible. Your HE is extremely effective in clearing out buildings and bunkers, but your AP will perform roughly similar to smaller calibers such as the 57mm 6 pounder AT gun due to the low muzzle velocity of the Shermans 75mm M3 gun.
For a medium tank, it is fast and maneuverable with good turret speed to give you even a bit more of an advantage in relatively short range engagements where you might otherwise be outclassed in gun performance.
